The '''1945–46 [[Super League Greece|Panhellenic Championship]]''' was the 12th season of the highest [[Association football|football]] league of Greece and the first after the [[World War II|WW2]]. The clubs that participated were the champions from the three founding football associations of the [[Hellenic Football Federation|HFF]]: [[Athens Football Clubs Association|Athens]], [[Piraeus Football Clubs Association|Piraeus]] and [[Macedonia Football Clubs Association|Macedonia]].

The championship was won by [[Aris Thessaloniki F.C.|Aris]] for their 3rd title. Initially, with the completion of all six matches, Aris held the first place in the standings. But then the HFF accepted the objections of their opponents for illegal use of the player Siotis (which he played in two clubs at the same season), awarding 2–0 in their favor, the last three of his four matches (an away draw against [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] and home wins against [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] and AEK), while at the same time zeroed the club of Thessaloniki for those matches. For a few days, the ranking was formed with the declaration of the AEK as champion by the HFF and Aris bringing the issue to its general assembly. In the end, Aris were vindicated in the appeal and won the title.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aek.com/AEKhistory/|title=Η ιστορία της ΑΕΚ|website=aek.com}}</ref> The point system was: ''Win: 3 points'' - ''Draw: 2 points'' - ''Loss: 1 point''.

*The championship was interrupted when on 19 May 1946 without the completion of the 15th matchday, while the replay matches were also postponed. The HFF declared the champions of Athens, Piraeus and Macedonia the first clubs of the standings, in order to participate in the Panhellenic championship.
